utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the Registrar call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-8-I, the Prosecutor versus Damir Dosen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, my name is Niemann, and I appear with my colleagues Mr. Keegan and Mr. Waidyaratne. Ms. Reynders is the case manager on this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If it please Your Honour, I appear on behalf of the defendant. My name is Michael Greaves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This matter has been listed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This matter has been listed for the initial appearance of this accused. Mr. Greaves, we understand that he does not attend due to injury.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. I went to the prison this morning in order to see him, and when I got there, I spoke with Mr. McFadden. He informed me that during the course of the weekend, the defendant, Mr. Dosen, had injured himself whilst engaged in physical activity and was at that stage in bed, on his back, and in receipt of treatment from a doctor, who was satisfied that he had got something wrong with his back and indicated that he was not fit to attend court today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm told it was due to playing volleyball.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes, so I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, the position is he's not here and obviously can't attend due to his medical condition. I'm told, too, that he could be here next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes. I had a brief discussion with Mr. McFadden. Obviously, he's not the doctor, but he relayed to me what the view was. As a result of that, I was going to suggest, and I hope this is a helpful suggestion, to perhaps aim at 9 o’clock next Monday morning in the hope that we shall be able to do something on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: In fact, the time that we had identified was 2.30, unless that makes any difference to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It would cause me difficulty because I have another commitment in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, all right. I recollect that I'm sitting at half past nine. Is it a case which is going to take very long?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: No. I was going to make what I hoped was a practical suggestion today, which would be that although he hasn't made his initial appearance, if the material which has to be disclosed could be made available to me fairly promptly, that will enable me to, I hope, shorten matters on Monday very, very quickly, and I would certainly give advice to my client that we needn't go through the business of reading the entire indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The only problem which occurs is the difficulty of finding a court next Monday at 9 o’clock. Mr. Niemann, as far as the Prosecution are concerned, is there any difficulty for next Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there's no difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn the matter until Monday, the 8th of November, at 9.00. Mr. Niemann, is there any difficulty in following the suggested course?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We could make this material available tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. I thank my learned friend for that. That would be extremely helpful, and then I will undertake, as far as I can, to see that the matter can last only about half an hour, if at all possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, are there any other matters to which we could deal with today?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It's a small practical suggestion. The indictment which I have has no enumeration to the counts on the indictment. They are, as it were, by paragraph, but that's slightly confusing because we start with paragraphs 1 to 10 or 1 to 11, which relate to other matters, and then the counts are contained within individual paragraphs. But the individual counts are not enumerated. I could see that leading to a degree of confusion in due course. I wonder whether my learned friend might care to, and I would be happy to agree in advance, to an amendment to add some numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: There may be, if Your Honour pleases, a number of versions of this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: That comes as no surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The version I have has numbered counts, and this is the one that has the blue cover. My friend has that one, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I've got a pretty blue cover as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But mine provides counts 1, 2, 3, through to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It may be I need to get back to the file of documents and try again. Thank you very much. I'm grateful to my friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. This matter is adjourned to next Monday at 9 o’clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: adjourned at 4.05 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 8th day of November, 1999, at 9 a.m.
